attempts.summary: Configured chrony on the RHEL 10 cluster so node1 acts as the internal time source and node2 syncs against it. On node1, edited /etc/chrony.conf to keep the public pool as node1's own upstream (so it has a real time reference) while adding `allow 10.100.93.11/32` (node2's IP) and `local stratum 10` as a fallback reference, then opened firewalld's ntp service. On node2, replaced the `pool 2.rhel.pool.ntp.org` directive with `server 10.100.93.10 iburst prefer`, pointing it at node1 exclusively. Verified node2 selects node1 (`^* 10.100.93.10`) as its best/only source and node1 lists node2 as an active NTP client. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured pre-restart boot_id and chrony state, issued `systemctl reboot` (ack returned before disconnect), polled until each node reconnected, confirmed changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on both (node1: e625b9a5→4c169d03; node2: 6d37896c→541128bd), and verified chronyd was active with the persisted config and the node1↔node2 sync relationship fully recovered after each restart (node2 tracking node1 via Reference ID 0A645D0A; node1 listing node2 as client) before moving to the next node.
